summary: Sporting News's Travis Pulver highlights six NFL award longshots for bettors to consider with five weeks left in the 2023 regular season, covering MVP, Offensive Player of the Year, Defensive Player of the Year, Coach of the Year and Comeback Player of the Year. For each award he names the current favorite(s) and argues why a lesser-backed candidate could still win. He advises keeping longshot bets small or using bonus bets, since payouts shrink as the season progresses.
one_line: Sporting News picks six NFL award longshots, including Stroud, Goff, Lamb, Hunter, Payton and Wilson, to consider betting with five weeks left in 2023.
key_facts: The article was published 2023-12-05 by Travis Pulver for Sporting News, with five weeks left in the regular season.
For MVP, the favorites after Week 13 are Brock Purdy, Dak Prescott and Jalen Hurts; the longshots are C.J. Stroud and Jared Goff.
Jared Goff's Lions are 9-3 and in contention for the No. 1 seed in the conference; the article says the Lions may have the easiest remaining schedule among the 49ers, Cowboys, Eagles and Lions.

C.J. Stroud leads the league in passing yards, is one of four quarterbacks with a passer rating over 100 who have started the whole season, and has the NFL's best touchdown-to-interception ratio (4 to 1).
Stroud's Texans had only 11 total wins over the last three seasons before becoming a playoff contender.

Tyreek Hill is the heavy OPOY favorite and is on track to be the first player with 2,000-plus receiving yards in a season; four of Miami's five remaining opponents have pass defenses ranked in the league's top eight.
CeeDee Lamb is on pace for close to 1,600 yards on his season average, or closer to 1,800 based on his last seven games, making him the OPOY longshot.
Danielle Hunter, the DPOY longshot, leads the league in tackles for a loss and is third in sacks with 13.5 behind Khalil Mack and T.J. Watt; the Vikings recovered from a 1-4 start.
The DPOY favorites are Micah Parsons, Myles Garrett and T.J. Watt.
For Coach of the Year, Dan Campbell is the favorite at +200 (DraftKings) and Sean Payton is the longshot at +2200 (DraftKings).

The article argues Campbell benefits from groundwork laid last season, while Payton turned around Denver's horrible start and resurrected Russell Wilson's career, though he may need to get Denver into the playoffs.
Damar Hamlin is the Comeback Player of the Year favorite after a cardiac arrest, but he has rarely played; Russell Wilson is the longshot.
Wilson had the league's best touchdown-to-interception ratio until a three-interception game the previous week, and it is still second-best.
